stem: Benzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$, reacts with chloroethane, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$, in the presence of a suitable catalyst to form ethylbenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$. In the presence of the catalyst, the ion $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5^+$ is formed. This ion reacts with benzene.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for the reaction of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ with this catalyst to form $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5^+$ as one product.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5^+ + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Ethylbenzene reacts with more $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$, forming a mixture containing 1,2-diethylbenzene and 1,4-diethylbenzene.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why there is very little 1,3-diethylbenzene in the product mixture.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
1,2-diethylbenzene can be oxidised to benzene-1,2-dioic acid, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{COOH})_2$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State the reagent and conditions used for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete the overall equation for this reaction.

An atom of oxygen from the oxidising agent is represented as [O].

All of the atoms in the two ethyl groups are fully oxidised in this reaction.

$$\ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots\text{[O]} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{COOH})_2 + \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

(1,2-diethylbenzene)

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Predict the number of peaks in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of benzene-1,2-dioic acid.
